messages:
maya: Quick sync: we keep hitting intermittent p95 token latency tails on /v1/generate and /v1/complete. Need a short plan to link metric spikes to traces without blowing up cardinality. High-level asks: (1) token-level breakdown by kernel, (2) per-route KPIs (p50/p95/p99) in one dashboard row, (3) a reliable way to jump from a metric spike to the exact trace/waterfall.

dmitri: Agreed. We've been blind to which kernel or scheduling event is responsible. Two complementary approaches: short-lived sampled request markers with trace_short + kernel label, and better kernel labels on the token histogram.

leela: Implementation constraints: we cannot add trace_id as a general metric label. Proposal: emit runtime_request_marker metric with labels {route, kernel_label, trace_short} sampled at 0.5% and TTL 60s. trace_short = first 8 chars of trace id to keep length small. This will let Grafana link to the trace store when investigating a spike.

jonah: PromQL examples for dashboards:
```
# token p95 by kernel
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_ms_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (kernel_label, le))

# batch wait average
sum(rate(runtime_batch_wait_ms_sum{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) / sum(rate(runtime_batch_wait_ms_count{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]))
```
Add a variable in Grafana `trace_short` that you can paste (from logs or request_marker) and a panel link to tracing UI querying by `trace_short`.

sara: On the logging side, ensure structured log lines include `req=` and `trace=` and host tags like `driver_version` and `thread_pool_queue_len`. Example log snippet we should standardize: 
```
2026-03-xxTxx:xx:xxZ runtime[req=rz2] trace=9c8f kernel=flash_k batch_size=1 kv_cache_hit=true token_ms=4.2 host=stg-gpu-07 driver_version=510.39
```
That allows quick grep -> paste into Grafana trace field.

nina: For the request_marker ingestion: simplest is push to our StatsD/Prometheus pipeline: increment a gauge runtime_request_marker{route, kernel_label, trace_short}=1 with a TTL recorder that expires after 60s. Make sure we sample 0.5% by default, configurable via env var.

dmitri: Regarding cardinality: we must strip user-provided data, restrict labels to route/kernel_label/host_group/trace_short, and limit sample rate. Estimate: at 0.5% on 10k rps that is ~50 markers/s -> 4320/day per cluster, acceptable in short bursts.

leela: Kernel labeling: we should export token latency histogram with kernel_label where available. If adding label is risky (cardinality) we can also export a separate metric `runtime_token_latency_by_kernel_ms_bucket{kernel_label,...}` and make it a lower-traffic metric (sampled or only on canary hosts).

jonah: Dashboard design specifics: one row per route with small panels left->right: p50/p95/p99 (histogram_quantile), next panel batch_wait_ms avg, next panel batch_size distribution heatmap, next panel kv_cache_hit_rate, final column: text input `trace_short` + button to fetch trace. Also include a waterfall panel that, given trace_short, queries traces and renders spans enqueue->batch_wait->dispatch->kernel_launch->token_emit.

maya: Good. We also need accept criteria for rollout:
- metric cardinality should not increase >5% after enabling markers (monitor prometheus_series_added)
- sampled markers appear in Grafana within 20s of request
- p95 investigations with markers reduce mean triage time by >=30% in pilot team (qualitative)

sara: Alerting tweaks: add an aggregate alert `route_token_latency_p95_by_kernel` to fire if p95 for any kernel_label > threshold for 3m. Also add `init_mutex_wait_ms` gauge and alert if >500ms for >1m on any host.

dmitri: For trace linking UX: implement an operational shortcut: when a dashboard spike is selected, show top `trace_short` values in the window (count of runtime_request_marker) and make them clickable to open the trace. That avoids manual copy/paste when markers exist.

leela: I'll prepare the guarded rollout: stage on canary pool first with kernel_label export and request_marker enabled at 0.5%. If stable after 2 hours, ramp to staging cluster and then prod. Will include config flags and a kill-switch env var.

jonah: I'll build the Grafana dashboard draft and add the `trace_short` variable + link to tracing UI. Will include example templated PromQL queries and a short playbook in the dashboard's help panel.

maya: Action items and owners:
- leela: proto and rollout plan for request_marker + guarded kernel_label export (PR by EOD)
- dmitri: add short PoC emitter in runtime that pushes runtime_request_marker at 0.5% sample rate (tomorrow)
- jonah: dashboard draft with trace_short UI and waterfall integration (tomorrow)
- sara: ensure logs include driver_version/thread_pool_queue_len and standardize the req/trace format (today)
- nina: monitor prometheus series cardinality after canary and sign off before prod ramp

perf-bot: creating incident ticket incident-2026-03-instr-req-trace-link.

maya: One more: let's include a small integration test in CI that simulates a kernel warmup path and asserts init_mutex_wait_ms metric is emitted. That will prevent regressions.

dmitri: I'll prototype hashed trace_short creation (first 8 hex chars) and a build flag to disable emission in CI/dev. We'll also add a Grafana helper that decodes trace_short to full trace lookup on the tracing service.

maya: This reads like a plan. Keep thread updates short. Paste PR links and dashboard link back here. If we can get markers + dashboard in next 48h, our triage time for token tails should drop significantly. Thanks team.
